chapter: Bebop, Tadd Dameron, Slam Stewart and Europe
title: Leaving Slam Stewart and laying off
summary: Slam and Beryl drank and Collins tired of managing them, so he quit and stopped playing professionally for a while.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Cole. I'd made many trips over there with him, though. We toured the whole -- we did the whole bit. But any way coming to Nat Cole, now, this is something else. I -- now, I won't go to Nat yet, I'll wait. I worked with Slam for a while, and Slam drank quite a bit, and so did Beryl Barrel, and it got to the point that I had to almost transport the group, you know, and see that they got to work. And I never liked that role, that wasn't my role.

And one night I just -- after the engagement I just packed up and left, couldn't stand it any longer. And I went to New York and I just decided to lay off for a while. I wouldn't play at all, I just -- not professionally. You know, I wouldn't accept any engagements. I just wanted to kind of regroup, get my thoughts together, and see what was happening with me.
